review.summary: Your resume has a clean, parser-friendly layout and correct chronological structure, which gives you a solid base to build on. The two changes that will move this furthest: cut the objective statement entirely (it reads as generic filler across every review) and rewrite your experience bullets to lead with strong past-tense action verbs and show outcomes rather than just duties. Alongside that, tightening the small consistency issues - the 'MY JOURNEY' heading, mixed date formats, the 'Finacial' typo, and missing GPA - will make the whole document read as more polished and finance-ready.
strengths: Reverse-chronological order within the experience entry is correct, and the one-page length fits the stage
Single-column plain-text layout with no tables, graphics, or text boxes, so a parser can read the content in order

dimensions.label: First impression
dimensions.notes: This reads as an early draft rather than a recruiting-ready document. The six-second scan lands on an objective statement, a section called 'MY JOURNEY', and a references line - none of which belong on a banking resume - before it even gets to substance.

issues.title: Objective statement wastes the top of page
issues.detail: The 'OBJECTIVE' block with 'incredibly passionate... leverage my skills' is filler a screener skips past. Delete it entirely and use that space for Education, which should be the first thing visible.

issues.title: No GPA, no highlights next to Education
issues.detail: Duke Economics entry has school, degree, and expected 2029 but no GPA. Screeners filter on GPA in the first pass - add it (and relevant coursework/honors if GPA is weak) directly under the degree line.

issues.title: References line and section title are off-convention
issues.detail: 'REFERENCES - Available upon request' is assumed and never included on finance resumes; cut it. Rename 'MY JOURNEY' to 'EXPERIENCE' - the casual label reads as unfamiliarity with the format.

issues.title: Unexplained gap and inconsistent dates
issues.detail: Internship ends Aug 2024 and the club role is dated 06/2023-09/2023, leaving gaps before and between with no freshman/sophomore-year activity shown. Also two date formats are used ('May 2024' vs '06/2023') - pick one and account for the timeline.

issues.title: Bullets state duties, not outcomes
issues.detail: All four bullets describe responsibilities ('maintaining the weekly dividend screen', 'presented stock pitches') with no result - no figure, decision made, or impact on client/team. A screener cannot tell if the work mattered.

issues.title: Weak opening verbs throughout
issues.detail: 'Responsible for maintaining' and 'Assisted with various research projects' open two bullets with passive, low-ownership language. Lead with a strong action verb (built, tracked, analyzed) that shows you did the work, not observed it.

issues.title: Inconsistent verb tense
issues.detail: 'Builds models' uses present tense while surrounding bullets use past tense for a completed internship. Keep all bullets in past tense for past roles to read as polished and consistent.

issues.title: Vague scope on research and pitches
issues.detail: 'Various research projects' and 'Presented stock pitches to the club' don't say how many, on what, or with what outcome (e.g., stock selected, thesis adopted). Name the specific company/sector and the result of the pitch.

issues.title: Non-standard section heading 'MY JOURNEY'
issues.detail: 'MY JOURNEY' replaces the standard 'EXPERIENCE' or 'WORK EXPERIENCE' heading. ATS parsers map content to fields using recognized headings; a custom label risks the whole section being dropped into an unparsed bucket or ignored entirely.

issues.title: Misspelled skill keyword 'Finacial'
issues.detail: The SKILLS line reads 'Finacial Modeling' - a typo. If a recruiter's ATS keyword search matches on 'Financial Modeling' exactly, the misspelling means this resume won't surface in that search even though the skill is genuinely listed.

issues.title: Inconsistent date formats across entries
issues.detail: Dates appear as 'May 2024 - Aug 2024' and '06/2023-09/2023' in the same document. Mixed formats can cause date-parsing fields in an ATS to misread or skip one entry, affecting how your tenure and recency are indexed.

issues.title: Objective reads generic, not finance-native
issues.detail: "Incredibly passionate and detail-oriented team player seeking a world-class finance internship where I can leverage my skills" uses inflated, content-free adjectives. A screener reads this as filler; IB/PE resumes either drop the summary entirely or state specific focus (sector, skill set, target function) in plain language.

issues.title: Skills list underselling and misspelled
issues.detail: "Finacial Modeling, Excel, PowerPoint" is a typo and reads as a generic office-skills list rather than finance craft. Fix the spelling and add specifics that signal real exposure, e.g. valuation methods, screening tools, or financial databases used.

issues.title: Objective is pure filler
issues.detail: Line 'Incredibly passionate and detail-oriented team player seeking a world-class finance internship where I can leverage my skills' is generic cliché that could sit on any resume. Cut the objective section entirely or replace with specific, factual content.3

issues.title: Inconsistent date formats
issues.detail: 'May 2024 - Aug 2024' under Pinecrest uses spelled-out months, while '06/2023-09/2023' under Duke Investment Club uses numeric slashes. Pick one format and apply it to both entries.

issues.title: Mixed verb tense on finished role
issues.detail: Pinecrest bullets mix tense: 'Responsible for maintaining,' 'Assisted with,' and 'Builds models' - the last is present tense for a completed May-Aug 2024 internship. Convert all three to past tense (e.g. 'Built').

issues.title: Spelling error in skills line
issues.detail: 'Finacial Modeling' under SKILLS is misspelled and will read as careless on a document meant to signal precision. Correct to 'Financial Modeling.'

rewrites.before: Responsible for maintaining the weekly dividend screen.
rewrites.after: Maintained a weekly dividend screen across [add figure: how many names/sectors?] stocks, flagging [add figure: how many] yield changes that fed into client review discussions.
rewrites.note: Lead with action verb, add scope and outcome.

rewrites.before: Assisted with various research projects for the consumer team.
rewrites.after: Researched [add detail: which subsector/companies?] for the consumer team, producing a comparable-company analysis that informed [add outcome: a pitch, a client memo?].
rewrites.note: Name the research and its downstream use.

rewrites.before: Builds models used in client portfolio reviews.
rewrites.after: Built valuation models used in client portfolio reviews, covering [add figure: how many client accounts or holdings?].
rewrites.note: Fix tense; add scale of usage.

rewrites.before: Presented stock pitches to the club.
rewrites.after: Pitched [add company name] to the Duke Investment Club, resulting in [add outcome: stock added to fund, top vote, etc.].
rewrites.note: Name the pitch and its result.

rewrites.before: Incredibly passionate and detail-oriented team player seeking a world-class finance internship where I can leverage my skills.
rewrites.after: Delete the objective section entirely, or replace with one line stating concrete focus, e.g. "Economics student focused on consumer sector equity research and financial modeling."
rewrites.note: Cut adjectives, state specific focus instead.

rewrites.after: Financial Modeling, Valuation (DCF, Comps), Excel, Bloomberg [confirm access], PowerPoint
rewrites.note: Fix spelling, add specific tools/methods used.
